newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Seed shortage may mean lower Brazil wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Seed shortage may mean lower Brazil wheat harvest.

text.p: Brazilian wheat production in 1997 could be hit by a shortage of certified seeds, said an analyst at the Agriculture Ministry's National Supply Company (Conab).
"According to the most recent information, 286,000 tonnes of seeds were used last year and this year we have only 223,000 tonnes available," said Paulo Rabelo.
"This is about 22 percent down from what was planted in 1996 and implies a reduction in output of 600,000 tonnes," he said.
According to Conab, Brazilian wheat output was 3.2 million tonnes in 1996, of which 500,000 tonnes are still to be sold.

One possibility is that farmers could use some of this wheat for seeding purposes, Rabelo said. He estimated that 63,000 tonnes of wheat would be sufficient to bring plantings back to the same level as in 1996.
Planting in some areas can start at the end of this month but in the key regions such as Parana and Rio Grande do Sul takes place from April and May.
Farmers are waiting to see the government's position re funding for the crop and what it will pay as a minimum price but this should only be decided by the end of March, Rabelo said.
"People are holding back a little because of the fall in world prices last year. But much will depend on the government's plans for the crop," Rabelo said.
While waiting to see how the government intends to help wheat farmers, independent consultants Safras e Mercado are already expecting to see a sharp fall in production from 1996.
In November last year, Safras said that output in 1997 could drop to 1.87 million tonnes and there has been little reason to change expectations, said analyst Gil Barabach.

"The feeling with regard to wheat production is not very good. Unless the government announces its plan for the winter crops quickly, the tendency is that production will fall drastically," Barabach said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
